name: Chotiwala
why_it_matters: Opened on 18 March 1958 in Swarg Ashram and grew into Rishikesh's most recognised pilgrim restaurant. After founder Agarwal died in 1990 the family split; in 1995 cousins Dinesh and Shailesh built a wall down the middle and now run two adjacent Chotiwalas — same logo, same name, identical fat-Brahmin mascot seated outside each entrance.
insider_tip: Both Chotiwalas are legitimate heirs — most regulars say the food is indistinguishable. Pick whichever has the shorter queue; the seated mascot will pose for a photo at either.
signature_address: Swarg Ashram, opposite Geeta Bhawan, Rishikesh 249304

name: Madras Cafe
why_it_matters: Tiny pure-veg cafe a minute from Ram Jhula taxi stand on The Mall Road — recently renovated, still serving the dosas-and-filter-coffee combo that locals send pilgrims to. Distinct from the unrelated Madras Cafe in Tapovan; this is the older Ram Jhula original near Andhra Ashram.
insider_tip: Profits from the small handicraft shop attached to the cafe go to GangaPrem Hospice — buy a wooden trinket on the way out if you liked the dosa.
signature_address: The Mall Road, near Andhra Ashram, Ram Jhula, Rishikesh 249201

name: Tulsi Restaurant
why_it_matters: Long-running Swarg Ashram multi-cuisine restaurant catering to ashram pilgrims and yoga-stay foreigners — the kind of veg menu that runs from south Indian to Chinese to muesli bowls without losing its kitchen. Plant-filled cosy interior, dim evening lighting, mains in the ₹160-200 range.
insider_tip: Reliable rather than thrilling — order south Indian or Garhwali. The continental and Chinese pages exist for the foreign-yoga-student audience.

name: Ganga Beach Cafe
why_it_matters: On Lakshman Jhula Road on the Swarg Ashram side, with a small stage where local and visiting musicians play through the evening. The riverside terrace is the reason to come — pizza and momos are decent, the Ganga view is the headline.
insider_tip: Show up around sunset; the cafe runs into the aarti hour and you can eat with the ghat lamps in view. The kitchen is slow when it's full — order before the live music starts.
signature_address: Lakshman Jhula Road, Swarg Ashram, Rishikesh 249304

name: The Office
why_it_matters: Tiny cafe off the main Swarg Ashram lane near Parmarth Niketan, with a five-table terrace looking over the Ganga. The eight-fruit muesli bowl and the apple-cinnamon samosa are why long-stay yoga students keep coming back.
insider_tip: Breakfast is the move — by 10am the terrace seats are gone. Cash only is the local convention; carry small notes.
signature_address: Swarg Ashram, near Parmarth Niketan Ashram, Rishikesh 249304

name: Hungry Yogi Health Cafe
why_it_matters: Quiet pure-veg health cafe in Swarg Ashram with a tofu-and-salad menu built for the resident yoga-school crowd. Free wifi, slow pace, fresh produce — long-stay students treat it as a workspace as much as a restaurant.
insider_tip: Vegan flags on the menu are accurate — they confirm before serving. Tofu options are made in-house and run out by late afternoon.
signature_address: Swarg Ashram, near Ram Jhula, Rishikesh 249304

name: Sanskriti Cafe
why_it_matters: One of the few Swarg Ashram cafes that takes Garhwali food seriously — kafuli, mandua roti, jhangora kheer cooked from scratch and served on a thali. River-facing seats, slow kitchen, no shortcuts.
insider_tip: Garhwali items take 30+ minutes — order them when you sit, get a chai while you wait. Skip the multi-cuisine pages and stay regional.
signature_address: Swarg Ashram, near Shivanand Hospital, Ram Jhula, Rishikesh 249304

name: Geeta Bhawan Bhojanalaya
why_it_matters: Geeta Bhawan, a major Swarg Ashram dharamshala run by Kalyan Trust, operates a community dining hall serving simple sattvic vegetarian meals to staying pilgrims and saints — donation-supported, no onion-garlic, fixed serving hours. One of the few places non-staying visitors can experience an old-school ashram bhojanalaya.
insider_tip: Hours are strict — breakfast around 8am, lunch noon-1pm, dinner before 8pm. Drop a donation in the daan-patra; staying guests eat free, walk-ins are expected to contribute.

name: Parmarth Niketan Ashram Canteen
why_it_matters: Parmarth Niketan — the largest ashram in Rishikesh and host of the Ganga aarti at Parmarth Ghat — runs a public canteen for both ashram residents and walk-in visitors. Plate is a fixed sattvic thali at roughly ₹70, served simple and clean from morning to late evening.
insider_tip: No-charge entry to the ashram complex; the canteen is open 6:30am-10:30pm so you can eat after the 6pm aarti without leaving the ghat. No alcohol, no non-veg, no onion-garlic on the plate — that's the rule, not a preference.
signature_address: Parmarth Niketan Ashram, Swarg Ashram, Rishikesh 249304

name: GMVN Ganga Resort Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam (GMVN) state-tourism property near Janki Setu / Ram Jhula. Live kitchen, vegetarian menu, complimentary unlimited buffet breakfast for guests, walk-in lunches and dinners for non-residents. The Garhwali breakfast is the reason to seek it out.
insider_tip: Walk-ins are accepted but call ahead during yatra season (Apr-Jun) — rooms fill, kitchen prioritises residents. The pathway from the resort connects to the Ram Jhula market in 5 minutes on foot.
signature_address: Muni Ki Reti, near Janki Setu, Ram Jhula, Rishikesh 249192
